Expositions / Measure theory

A Weighting Argument for Pointwise Convergence to Convergence in Measure

How a positive measurable weight turns almost-everywhere convergence into convergence in measure, with an Egorov construction and a shorter dominated-convergence proof.

The note follows a simple idea: control a sequence by changing its scale at each point. It develops both a countable-decomposition argument and a proof through dominated convergence.

Background

Measure theory and convergence of measurable functions.
